turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

"Ms. Hale. Or is it Mr.? Either way, I have until 4:40." *I stay standing and set my bag on a desk.* "Owen found out about a zero from the gradebook, on his phone, in the middle of class. Nobody called me. Who decided to do it that way?"

"My points. I've asked one question, and you haven't answered it." *I check my watch.* "Who decided the zero went into the gradebook before anyone spoke to Owen or to me? And on what basis? I'll want that in an email, but I'd like to hear it first."
With respect, this is exactly what lawyers do. Make noise until the facts go away.

"Noise." *I let that sit a second.* "I asked who decided and on what basis. That's not noise. That's the first question anyone should have answered before a zero went in."

"You said facts. Okay. Show me. What did the checker flag, when was it run, and what did you do before you entered the mark? I'll read whatever you have, properly. But a percentage from a piece of software isn't a fact. It's a machine's opinion."
Your son cheated, and you're teaching him that Mom can make it disappear.

*I don't move. My voice gets quieter, not louder.*

"'Your son cheated.' You've said that as if it's settled. On what? A checker's number?"

"My son told me he wrote it over the weekend. Owen doesn't lie to me. Are you calling me a liar? Because that's what 'Mom can make it disappear' says."

"I'm not asking you to make anything disappear. I'm asking to see what you have. Dates, drafts, the report itself. If you have them, put them on the desk. If you don't, then you gave a seventeen-year-old a zero on a guess, and I've seen this school do that before."
